case_name: Chigurupati Sambasiva Rao v. Chigurupati Vijayalakshmi
facts_of_case: The husband filed for divorce under Section 13(1)(ib) of the Hindu Marriage Act on grounds of desertion. The wife denied all allegations and left her husband's company multiple times without reasonable cause.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the petitioner to establish that the respondent deserted him without any reasonable cause and without his consent for not less than two years immediately preceding the presentation of the petition.
legal_principles.held: When he failed to discharge such burden, the petition must fail.

legal_principles.principle: The petitioner must adduce positive evidence to establish the fact that the respondent had left his company two years prior to filing of the petition.
legal_principles.held: When he failed to discharge such burden, the petition must fail.

legal_principles.principle: The non-examination of any of the neighbours is one of the circumstances which goes against the petitioner.
legal_principles.held: But, the petitioner did not choose to examine not even a single person who resides in the locality where the house of the petitioner is situated.

legal_principles.principle: The principle of burden of proof applies to the petitioner seeking a decree of divorce on the ground of desertion.
legal_principles.held: When he failed to discharge such burden, the petition must fail.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order dismissing the petition for divorce was upheld, and the appeal was rejected.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for judicial separation
